thinking_and_logic: Your final approach uses a single pass through the array while storing previously seen values mapped to their indices. For each number n at index i, you compute complement = target - n and check if it has been seen; if so, you return the prior index and i. Checking before inserting guarantees you don’t reuse the same element, and it naturally handles duplicates by keeping an index for each seen value.
code_assessment: Your solution is effectively identical to the answer key’s optimal approach (single-pass hash map). The key interview-critical detail—checking the complement before inserting the current element—avoids the “use the same element twice” pitfall. Compared to brute force O(n^2), your code achieves O(n) time and scales to 1e5 elements; it also avoids the common incorrect approach of sorting and losing original indices.
